strengths: The neon cyan palette is coherent, and bloom on the arena walls gives a clear synthwave look
The HUD is cohesive: three matching glass-style panels for score, best and level, plus styled title and game-over cards with a 'NEW BEST!' message
Sparks appear on eating and on death, and the snake fades from a bright head to a teal tail
Stable at runtime: 0 page errors, 12/13 browser checks passed, and the autopilot ate 22 foods in 40 s
The perspective camera shows the board as a real 3D plane, and motion between frames looks smooth
weaknesses: 'Enter starts a new game at once' fails, so restarting after game over is clumsy
The snake is plain cubes and the food is a small, faint pink disk that is hard to see on the board
Bloom overexposes the edges: when the snake runs along the top wall it washes into the glow and is hard to read
Little real 3D depth: almost no visible shadows, no modeled shapes, and the floor is a flat checkerboard
On a phone the board takes up only a small strip with lots of empty space, and the title card covers it
The eating effect is barely visible (a few tiny sparks), and the only theme touch is the generic neon
oneLine: A tidy, stable neon snake with a good HUD, but its plain shapes, faint food, washed-out bloom and slow restart make it look more like a polished demo than a finished indie game.
